title_en: A day of reading: the capstone
q_en: Can I read any text, of any kind, and understand it?
q_ar: هَلْ أَقْرَأُ أَيَّ نَصٍّ مِنْ أَيِّ نَوْعٍ وَأَفْهَمُهُ؟
not_yet: Kinds of text this course did not show: you now have the questions to meet them.
Every new word: keep a list and look it up by its root.
Reading fast, reading aloud with ease, and reading handwriting: practice gives you these, not a lesson.
not_yet_ar: أَنْوَاعٌ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ لَمْ يُرِكَ الْكِتَابُ إِيَّاهَا: مَعَكَ الْآنَ أَسْئِلَةٌ تَفْتَحُهَا.
كُلُّ كَلِمَةٍ جَدِيدَةٍ: اُكْتُبْهَا فِي قَائِمَةٍ وَاطْلُبْهَا مِنْ جَذْرِهَا.
الْقِرَاءَةُ السَّرِيعَةُ وَالْقِرَاءَةُ بِصَوْتٍ عَالٍ وَقِرَاءَةُ الْخَطِّ الْيَدَوِيِّ: تَأْتِي بِالتَّمْرِينِ لَا بِالدَّرْسِ.

slides.big_en: Fifteen kinds of text. Ten questions. One reader: you.
slides.small: There is no new grammar today. You read a whole day of texts you have not seen.
slides.small_ar: لَا قَاعِدَةَ جَدِيدَةً الْيَوْمَ. تَقْرَأُ يَوْمًا كَامِلًا مِنَ النُّصُوصِ الْجَدِيدَةِ.

slides.head_en: Look: six lines, six kinds of text
sents: It was announced: a new match. (a news report)
Ingredients: a cup of flour. (a recipe)
زَعَمُوا أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ فِي الْوَادِي.
They claim that a monkey was in the wadi. (a fable)
To proceed: I am well. (a letter)
بَاعَ سَالِمٌ دَارَهُ بِثَمَنٍ قَدْرُهُ مِائَةُ رِيَالٍ.
Sālim sold his house for a price amounting to a hundred riyals. (a contract)

lines: Which word in each line told you the kind of text?
أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ فِي كُلِّ سَطْرٍ دَلَّتْكَ عَلَى نَوْعِ النَّصِّ؟
Did you need to read the whole line? (Look at the first two words.)
هَلْ احْتَجْتَ إِلَى قِرَاءَةِ السَّطْرِ كُلِّهِ؟ (اُنْظُرْ إِلَى أَوَّلِ كَلِمَتَيْنِ.)
Which lines begin with a verb, and which have no verb at all?
أَيُّ الْأَسْطُرِ يَبْدَأُ بِفِعْلٍ؟ وَأَيُّهَا لَيْسَ فِيهِ فِعْلٌ؟

cards.def_ar: اِقْرَأْ أَوَّلَ كَلِمَتَيْنِ وَانْظُرْ إِلَى شَكْلِ الصَّفْحَةِ.
cards.def_en: Read the first two words and look at the shape of the page.
Who? What? When? Why? Ten questions open any text.

cards.def_ar: قُلْ مَعْنَى النَّصِّ فِي سَطْرٍ وَاحِدٍ.
cards.def_en: Say what it means in one line, in English and in Arabic.

slides.note: You met five questions in Lesson 39. Now there are ten.
slides.note_ar: تَعَلَّمْتَ خَمْسَةَ أَسْئِلَةٍ فِي الدَّرْسِ ٣٩. وَالْآنَ عَشَرَةٌ.

rows: What does it want from me?
slides.note: Questions 1–3 are about the whole text. Questions 4–6 are about its words and joints. Questions 7–10 take the meaning out.
slides.note_ar: ١–٣ عَنِ النَّصِّ كُلِّهِ. ٤–٦ عَنِ الْكَلِمَاتِ وَالرَّبْطِ. ٧–١٠ لِاسْتِخْرَاجِ الْمَعْنَى.

slides.head_en: Fifteen kinds of text: the tradition
rows: a source line · قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ
short · a number and a list
slides.note: The same kinds as the first level of the ladder: you can now read each one without vowels.
slides.note_ar: هَذِهِ الْأَنْوَاعُ نَفْسُهَا، وَتَقْرَؤُهَا الْآنَ بِلَا حَرَكَاتٍ.

slides.head_en: Fifteen kinds of text: the world
rows: أَمَّا بَعْدُ · the greeting · the closing
slides.note: Eight kinds, and each one has a few words that open it.
slides.note_ar: ثَمَانِيَةُ أَنْوَاعٍ، وَلِكُلِّ نَوْعٍ كَلِمَاتٌ تَفْتَحُهُ.

rows: one word: its kind, its root and pattern
of, his, and, who, because, numbers
a story, a dialogue, a ḥadīth, the Qur’an
slides.note: Lesson 1: “Three kinds of word”. Lesson 39: “Read and understand”.
slides.note_ar: الدَّرْسُ ١: أَنْوَاعُ الْكَلِمَةِ. الدَّرْسُ ٣٩: اِقْرَأْ وَافْهَمْ.

rows: through the shape to the root; the passive; forms I–X
state, reason, calling, “if”, numbers and dates
tafsīr, ḥadīth, matn, counsel, litany, mawlid, qaṣīda, sīra, fatwā
news, forms, recipes, fables, proverbs, travel, contracts
slides.note: From Level 8 the vowels fade; at Level 9 you read without them.
slides.note_ar: مِنَ الْمُسْتَوَى الثَّامِنِ تَخْتَفِي الْحَرَكَاتُ، وَفِي التَّاسِعِ تَقْرَأُ بِدُونِهَا.

slides.wrong: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ قِرْدًا كَانَ فِي الْوَادِي
slides.why: A student translates: “They lied that a monkey was in the wadi.” Wrong! زَعَمُوا opens a tale: “They say that … / Once upon a time …”.
slides.why_ar: تَرْجَمَ طَالِبٌ: «كَذَبُوا». هَذَا خَطَأٌ! تَفْتَحُ «زَعَمُوا» الْحِكَايَةَ: «يُقَالُ إِنَّ … / كَانَ يَا مَا كَانَ …».

slides.head_en: The last lesson: the boy teaches
lines: قَالَ الْوَلَدُ الصَّغِيرُ: لَا أَفْهَمُ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ.
The little boy said: I do not understand this book.
جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَهُ وَقَالَ: اِقْرَأْ، ثُمَّ اسْأَلْ: مَا نَوْعُهُ؟ وَمَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ؟
Ahmad sat with him and said: Read, then ask: What kind is it? Who is speaking?
وَمَاذَا يَقُولُ؟ وَمَاذَا يُرِيدُ مِنِّي؟
And what does it say? And what does it want from me?
ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ: اِقْرَأْ وَافْهَمْ.
Then he said to him: Read and understand.

slides.small: You started with one word. You can now read a day of texts. Now do the last exercise.
slides.small_ar: بَدَأْتَ بِكَلِمَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ، وَتَقْرَأُ الْآنَ يَوْمًا مِنَ النُّصُوصِ. الْآنَ التَّمْرِينُ الْأَخِيرُ.

can: I can tell what kind of text I am reading, and say how I know.
I can read a Qur’an verse, a ḥadīth and a short matn, and say what they mean.
I can read counsel, a line of poetry, mawlid prose and a proverb.
I can read a letter, a news report, a form and a recipe.
I can read a fable, an encyclopaedia entry, a travel story and a contract.
I can use the reader’s ten questions on any text.
I can find the root of a word and guess its meaning from it.
I can translate a line into English, and write a line in Arabic in the style of its kind.
I can read without vowels and put the vowels in my head.
I can teach a younger reader the first lesson: اِقْرَأْ وَافْهَمْ.
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَعْرِفَ نَوْعَ النَّصِّ الَّذِي أَقْرَؤُهُ وَأَقُولَ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتُ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ آيَةً وَحَدِيثًا وَمَتْنًا قَصِيرًا وَأَقُولَ مَعْنَاهَا.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ نَصِيحَةً وَبَيْتَ شِعْرٍ وَنَثْرَ الْمَوْلِدِ وَمَثَلًا.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ رِسَالَةً وَخَبَرًا وَاسْتِمَارَةً وَطَرِيقَةَ طَعَامٍ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ حِكَايَةً وَمَادَّةً مِنْ مَوْسُوعَةٍ وَرِحْلَةً وَعَقْدًا.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْتَعْمِلَ أَسْئِلَةَ الْقَارِئِ الْعَشَرَةَ فِي أَيِّ نَصٍّ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَجِدَ جَذْرَ الْكَلِمَةِ وَأُخَمِّنَ مَعْنَاهَا مِنْهُ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُتَرْجِمَ سَطْرًا إِلَى الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّةِ وَأَكْتُبَ سَطْرًا بِالْعَرَبِيَّةِ عَلَى أُسْلُوبِ نَوْعِهِ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ بِلَا حَرَكَاتٍ وَأَضَعَ الْحَرَكَاتِ فِي ذِهْنِي.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أُعَلِّمَ قَارِئًا أَصْغَرَ الدَّرْسَ الْأَوَّلَ: اِقْرَأْ وَافْهَمْ.

sections.name: A
sections.en: Dawn. A verse of the Qur’an, from the wird. Read it aloud, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: فَإِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
For indeed, with hardship comes ease.
إِنَّ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ يُسْرًا
Indeed, with hardship comes ease.
sections.cite: Qur’an 94:5–6 (Sūrat al-Sharḥ); the text is taken by program from the course Qur’an file.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
options: The Qur’an: Sūrat al-Sharḥ (94), verses 5 and 6.
items.answer: The Qur’an: Sūrat al-Sharḥ (94), verses 5 and 6.
items.model: The Qur’an: Sūrat al-Sharḥ (94), verses 5 and 6.

items.en: Which two words are opposites?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ كَلِمَتَيْنِ مُتَضَادَّتَانِ؟
options: The Qur’an: Sūrat al-Sharḥ (94), verses 5 and 6.
items.model: الْعُسْرِ (hardship) and يُسْرًا (ease).

items.en: Which little word says that the ease comes with the hardship, and not after it?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الْيُسْرَ مَعَ الْعُسْرِ لَا بَعْدَهُ؟
options: The Qur’an: Sūrat al-Sharḥ (94), verses 5 and 6.
items.model: مَعَ (“with”).

items.en: ★ The same sentence comes in verse 5 and in verse 6. What does the repeating do?
items.ar_q: ★ تَتَكَرَّرُ الْجُمْلَةُ فِي الْآيَتَيْنِ. مَاذَا يُفِيدُ التَّكْرَارُ؟
items.model: It makes the promise firm; the reader is meant to hear it twice.

items.en: ★ What does this text want from the reader? Say it in one line.
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا يُرِيدُ النَّصُّ مِنَ الْقَارِئِ؟ قُلْهُ فِي سَطْرٍ وَاحِدٍ.
items.model: It comforts: do not lose hope in hardship, for ease comes with it.

sections.name: B
sections.en: After the dawn prayer. A ḥadīth. Read it aloud, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: وَاللَّهِ إِنِّي لَأَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ فِي الْيَوْمِ أَكْثَرَ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً
By God, I ask God’s forgiveness and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day.
sections.cite: al-Bukhārī, al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Dār al-Shaʿb, Cairo, 1st ed. 1407 H / 1987, Fatḥ al-Bārī numbering (Shamela 1782), no. 6307, 8/83. The words of the Prophet ﷺ; the print omits one fatḥa (on the lām of لَأَسْتَغْفِرُ), added by the course.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: A ḥadīth, from Ṣaḥīḥ al-Bukhārī (no. 6307), narrated by Abū Hurayra.

items.en: Who is speaking? (Look at the source line.)
items.ar_q: مَنِ الْمُتَكَلِّمُ؟ (اُنْظُرْ إِلَى سَطْرِ الْمَصْدَرِ.)
items.model: The Prophet ﷺ; Abū Hurayra reports his words.

items.en: How many times a day? Find the words.
items.ar_q: كَمْ مَرَّةً فِي الْيَوْمِ؟ جِدِ الْكَلِمَاتِ.
items.model: More than seventy times: أَكْثَرَ مِنْ سَبْعِينَ مَرَّةً.

items.en: ★ What do the two verbs mean, and what is the difference?
items.ar_q: ★ مَا مَعْنَى الْفِعْلَيْنِ؟ وَمَا الْفَرْقُ بَيْنَهُمَا؟
items.model: أَسْتَغْفِرُ: I ask forgiveness (root غ ف ر); أَتُوبُ: I turn back in repentance (root ت و ب). The first asks; the second returns.

items.en: ★ What does this ḥadīth want from the reader? Say it in one line.
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا يُرِيدُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثُ مِنَ الْقَارِئِ؟ قُلْهُ فِي سَطْرٍ.
items.model: It teaches by example: ask God’s forgiveness and turn back to Him many times a day.

sections.name: C
sections.en: Morning lesson. A matn (three short lines). Read it, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: أَعْذَارُ الصَّلَاةِ اثْنَانِ: النَّوْمُ وَالنِّسْيَانُ.
The excuses for the prayer are two: sleep and forgetting.
الْأَحْدَاثُ اثْنَانِ: أَصْغَرُ وَأَكْبَرُ.
The states of impurity are two: the minor and the major.
فَالْأَصْغَرُ مَا أَوْجَبَ الْوُضُوءَ، وَالْأَكْبَرُ مَا أَوْجَبَ الْغُسْلَ.
The minor is what requires wuḍūʾ, and the major is what requires the full wash.

items.model: A matn (a short text of fiqh, to be learned by heart): Safīnat al-Najā of Sālim b. Sumayr al-Ḥaḍramī.

items.en: Line 1: what are the two excuses for the prayer?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ١: مَا الْعُذْرَانِ لِلصَّلَاةِ؟

Two: the minor (أَصْغَرُ) and the major

items.en: Line 2: how many kinds of ḥadath (impurity) are there, and which?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٢: كَمْ نَوْعًا لِلْحَدَثِ؟ وَمَا هِيَ؟

The minor requires wuḍūʾ; the major requires the full wash

items.model: Two: the minor (أَصْغَرُ) and the major (أَكْبَرُ).

items.en: Line 3: which kind requires wuḍūʾ, and which requires the full wash?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٣: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ يُوجِبُ الْوُضُوءَ؟ وَأَيُّ نَوْعٍ يُوجِبُ الْغُسْلَ؟

items.ar_q: ★ لِلسَّطْرَيْنِ ١ وَ٢ قَالَبٌ وَاحِدٌ. اُكْتُبْهُ.

items.en: ★ Why is a matn so short, and where does the explanation come from?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا الْمَتْنُ قَصِيرٌ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ يَأْتِي الشَّرْحُ؟
items.model: A matn is short so that it can be learned by heart; the explanation is in a commentary (sharḥ) read with a teacher.

sections.name: D
sections.en: Counsel. One line of wisdom. Read it, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: لَيْسَ وَاضِعُ الْمَالِ فِي غَيْرِ حَقِّهِ بِأَقَلَّ إِثْمًا مِنْ مَاسِكِهِ عَنْ حَقِّهِ.
One who puts wealth where it does not belong is no less sinful than one who withholds it from its due.

sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: Counsel (a ḥikma, a short saying of wisdom), from Kitāb al-Ḥikam of Imam ʿAbdallāh b. ʿAlawī al-Ḥaddād.

items.en: Who are the two men in the line?
items.ar_q: مَنِ الرَّجُلَانِ فِي السَّطْرِ؟
items.model: The one who puts wealth where it does not belong (وَاضِعُ الْمَالِ فِي غَيْرِ حَقِّهِ) and the one who holds it back from its due (مَاسِكُهُ عَنْ حَقِّهِ).

items.en: Which word means “sin”, and which means “less”?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «الذَّنْبَ»؟ وَأَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «أَدْنَى»؟
items.model: إِثْمًا (sin); أَقَلَّ (less).

items.en: Does the line praise the one who withholds wealth, or the one who puts it in the wrong place?
items.ar_q: هَلْ يَمْدَحُ السَّطْرُ مَنْ يُمْسِكُ الْمَالَ أَمْ مَنْ يَضَعُهُ فِي غَيْرِ حَقِّهِ؟
items.model: Neither: it blames both. The first is “not less sinful” than the second.

items.en: ★ How does لَيْسَ work here? Why is there a بِ before أَقَلَّ?
items.ar_q: ★ كَيْفَ تَعْمَلُ «لَيْسَ» هُنَا؟ لِمَاذَا جَاءَتِ الْبَاءُ قَبْلَ «أَقَلَّ»؟
items.model: لَيْسَ takes بِ before its predicate. “X is not less sinful than Y” (أَقَلَّ إِثْمًا مِنْ): a negated comparison.

items.en: ★ What does the line want from the reader? Say it in one line.
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا يُرِيدُ السَّطْرُ مِنَ الْقَارِئِ؟ قُلْهُ فِي سَطْرٍ.
items.model: Put wealth where it belongs: do not waste it and do not hold it back.

sections.name: E
sections.en: Poetry. One bayt: two halves, read as two lines. Read it aloud, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: مَا كُلُّ مَا يَتَمَنَّى الْمَرْءُ يُدْرِكُهُ
Not everything a man wishes for does he reach:
تَجْرِي الرِّيَاحُ بِمَا لَا تَشْتَهِي السُّفُنُ
the winds blow in ways the ships do not desire.
sections.cite: Abū l-Ṭayyib al-Mutanabbī, Dīwān, Shamela 3.28 id 6707, p. 134 of the copy (last bayt shown on that page; pagination UNSURE, as above); also in al-Wāḥidī's Sharḥ (3.28 id 6553, digital p. 332). Famous proverb-like bayt.. Vowels: the course’s (vowelled for learners).
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: مَا نَوْعُ هَذَا النَّصِّ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: A bayt of poetry (two halves) by al-Mutanabbī, from his Dīwān.

items.en: Translate the first half.
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ الشَّطْرَ الْأَوَّلَ.
items.model: Not everything a man wishes for does he reach;

items.en: Translate the second half.
items.ar_q: تَرْجِمِ الشَّطْرَ الثَّانِيَ.
items.model: the winds blow in ways the ships do not desire.

items.en: In the picture, who are the ships and what are the winds?
items.ar_q: فِي الصُّورَةِ: مَنِ السُّفُنُ؟ وَمَا الرِّيَاحُ؟
items.model: The ships are people with their wishes; the winds are what happens, which does not follow their wishes.

items.en: ★ Which half carries the rhyme? How can you tell this is verse and not prose?
items.ar_q: ★ أَيُّ الشَّطْرَيْنِ فِيهِ الْقَافِيَةُ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ أَنَّهُ شِعْرٌ لَا نَثْرٌ؟
items.model: The second half ends in السُّفُنُ (rhyme: nūn). It is one line in two halves, built on a picture, not a report.

items.en: ★ What does the line want from the reader? Say it in one line.
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا يُرِيدُ الْبَيْتُ مِنَ الْقَارِئِ؟ قُلْهُ فِي سَطْرٍ.
items.model: It teaches calm: things do not always go as we wish, and that is part of life.

sections.name: F
sections.en: The night of the mawlid. Mawlid prose (rhymed clauses). Read it aloud, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْنَا نَبِيَّهُ رَحْمَةً، وَجَعَلَ ذِكْرَهُ لِلْقُلُوبِ نِعْمَةً.
Praise be to God, who sent us His Prophet as a mercy and made remembering him a blessing for hearts.
اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ، صَلَاةً تَغْفِرُ لَنَا بِهَا الذُّنُوبَ، وَتَجْمَعُ بِهَا الْقُلُوبَ.
O God, send blessings and peace upon our master Muḥammad ﷺ, a blessing by which You forgive us our sins and bring hearts together.
وَهَذِهِ لَيْلَةُ الْمَوْلِدِ، فَاجْتَمَعْنَا فِيهَا مَعَ الْإِخْوَانِ، نَقْرَأُ وَنَسْمَعُ وَنَذْكُرُ نَبِيَّنَا ﷺ.
And this is the night of the mawlid, so we gathered in it with our brothers, reading, listening and remembering our Prophet ﷺ.
sections.cite: Course text written for this lesson (generic; no real person, institution or number). Written in the register of mawlid prose (balanced clauses, rhymed endings).
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: Line 1: what did God send us, and what did He make a blessing?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ١: مَاذَا أَرْسَلَ اللَّهُ إِلَيْنَا؟ وَمَاذَا جَعَلَ نِعْمَةً؟
items.model: He sent us His Prophet as a mercy, and made remembering him a blessing for hearts.

items.en: Line 2: what do we ask God for?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٢: مَاذَا نَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ؟
items.model: To send blessings and peace upon our master Muḥammad ﷺ, by which He forgives our sins and brings hearts together.

items.en: Line 3: what do the people do on the night of the mawlid?
items.ar_q: السَّطْرُ ٣: مَاذَا يَفْعَلُ النَّاسُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْمَوْلِدِ؟
items.model: They gather with their brothers: they read, listen and remember their Prophet ﷺ.

items.en: ★ Find the words that end alike in lines 1 and 2. What is this style called?
items.ar_q: ★ جِدِ الْكَلِمَاتِ الَّتِي تَنْتَهِي بِصَوْتٍ وَاحِدٍ فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ ١ وَ٢. مَا اسْمُ هَذَا الْأُسْلُوبِ؟
items.model: رَحْمَةً / نِعْمَةً and الذُّنُوبَ / الْقُلُوبَ: rhymed prose (sajʿ), the style of mawlid texts.

items.en: ★ Say the whole text in one line.
items.ar_q: ★ قُلِ النَّصَّ كُلَّهُ فِي سَطْرٍ وَاحِدٍ.
items.model: It praises God for sending the Prophet ﷺ as a mercy, asks for blessings upon him, and tells of the gathering of the night of the mawlid.

sections.name: G
sections.en: A letter comes. Read it, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate
مِنْ سَالِمٍ إِلَى ابْنِ أَخِيهِ أَحْمَدَ
From Sālim to his nephew Aḥmad
السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ وَرَحْمَةُ اللَّهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، أَمَّا بَعْدُ:
Peace be upon you, and God’s mercy and blessings. To proceed:
فَوَصَلَتْنِي رِسَالَتُكَ وَأَنَا سَعِيدٌ بِهَا.
Your letter reached me and I am happy with it.
وَأَنَا أُرْسِلُ إِلَيْكَ كِتَابًا جَدِيدًا، فَاقْرَأْهُ مَعَ عُمَرَ.
I am sending you a new book; read it with ʿUmar.
وَاجْتَهِدْ فِي الدَّرْسِ، وَاكْتُبْ إِلَيَّ كُلَّ شَهْرٍ.
Strive in your lesson, and write to me every month.
وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكَ. عَمُّكَ سَالِمٌ.
And peace be upon you. Your uncle Sālim.
sections.cite: Course text written for this lesson (generic; no real person, institution or number). Written in the register of a classical letter (basmala, “from … to …”, greeting, أَمَّا بَعْدُ, closing).
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: Who writes to whom?
items.ar_q: مَنْ يَكْتُبُ إِلَى مَنْ؟
items.model: Sālim (the uncle) writes to his nephew Aḥmad.

items.en: Which line is the greeting, and which words begin the message itself?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ سَطْرٍ هُوَ التَّحِيَّةُ؟ وَبِأَيِّ كَلِمَاتٍ تَبْدَأُ الرِّسَالَةُ؟
items.model: Line 3 is the greeting; the message begins after أَمَّا بَعْدُ.

items.en: What did the uncle receive, and what does he send?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا وَصَلَ الْعَمَّ؟ وَمَاذَا يُرْسِلُ؟
items.model: He received Aḥmad’s letter and is happy with it; he sends a new book.

items.en: ★ What three things does the uncle ask of Aḥmad?
items.ar_q: ★ مَا الْأُمُورُ الثَّلَاثَةُ الَّتِي يَطْلُبُهَا الْعَمُّ؟
items.model: To read the book with ʿUmar, to strive in his lesson, and to write to him every month.

items.en: ★ Name three signs that this is a letter.
items.ar_q: ★ اُذْكُرْ ثَلَاثَ عَلَامَاتٍ تَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ النَّصَّ رِسَالَةٌ.
items.model: The basmala; “from … to …”; the greeting and أَمَّا بَعْدُ; the closing وَالسَّلَامُ and the signature.

sections.name: H
sections.en: News from the town. Read it, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: رِحْلَةٌ لِطُلَّابِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ إِلَى السَّاحِلِ
A trip for the school’s students to the coast
الْمَدِينَةُ – أُعْلِنَ أَمْسِ عَنْ رِحْلَةٍ لِطُلَّابِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ إِلَى السَّاحِلِ يَوْمَ الْأَحَدِ.
The town – It was announced yesterday that there will be a trip for the school’s students to the coast on Sunday.
وَتَخْرُجُ السَّيَّارَةُ فِي السَّاعَةِ ٦:٣٠ صَبَاحًا مِنْ أَمَامِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
The car leaves at 6:30 in the morning from in front of the school.
وَقَالَ الْمُعَلِّمُ إِنَّ عَلَى كُلِّ طَالِبٍ أَنْ يَحْمِلَ الْمَاءَ، وَإِنَّ الرِّحْلَةَ تَرْجِعُ بَعْدَ الْعَصْرِ.
The teacher said that every student must carry water, and that the trip returns after the afternoon.
sections.cite: Course text written for this lesson (generic; no real person, institution or number). Written in the register of a news report (headline, dateline, passive أُعْلِنَ).
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: What is the headline about?
items.ar_q: عَنْ مَاذَا الْعُنْوَانُ؟
options: It was announced yesterday; the trip is on Sunday.
A trip for the school’s students to the coast.
At 6:30 in the morning, from in front of the school.
items.answer: A trip for the school’s students to the coast.
items.model: A trip for the school’s students to the coast.

items.en: When was it announced, and on which day is the trip?
items.ar_q: مَتَى أُعْلِنَ الْخَبَرُ؟ وَفِي أَيِّ يَوْمٍ الرِّحْلَةُ؟
options: At 6:30 in the morning, from in front of the school.
It was announced yesterday; the trip is on Sunday.
A trip for the school’s students to the coast.
items.answer: It was announced yesterday; the trip is on Sunday.
items.model: It was announced yesterday; the trip is on Sunday.

items.en: At what time does the car leave, and from where?
items.ar_q: فِي أَيِّ سَاعَةٍ تَخْرُجُ السَّيَّارَةُ؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ؟
options: It was announced yesterday; the trip is on Sunday.
A trip for the school’s students to the coast.
At 6:30 in the morning, from in front of the school.
items.answer: At 6:30 in the morning, from in front of the school.
items.model: At 6:30 in the morning, from in front of the school.

items.en: What must every student carry, and when does the trip return?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا يَحْمِلُ كُلُّ طَالِبٍ؟ وَمَتَى تَرْجِعُ الرِّحْلَةُ؟
options: It was announced yesterday; the trip is on Sunday.
A trip for the school’s students to the coast.
At 6:30 in the morning, from in front of the school.
items.model: Water; after the afternoon (after ʿaṣr).

items.en: ★ Is أُعْلِنَ active or passive? Why does a news report often use it?
items.ar_q: ★ هَلْ «أُعْلِنَ» مَعْلُومٌ أَمْ مَجْهُولٌ؟ لِمَاذَا يَكْثُرُ فِي الْأَخْبَارِ؟
items.model: Passive: “it was announced”. The announcer is not named; the news is the point.

items.en: ★ What does the report want from its readers?
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا يُرِيدُ الْخَبَرُ مِنَ الْقُرَّاءِ؟
items.model: That the students and their families know the day and the time, and bring water.

sections.name: I
sections.en: At the library door. A form and a notice. Read them, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: اِسْتِمَارَةُ التَّسْجِيلِ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ
Library registration form
يُرْجَى كِتَابَةُ الِاسْمِ وَالْعُنْوَانِ كِتَابَةً وَاضِحَةً.
Please write the name and the address clearly.
مَمْنُوعٌ اللَّعِبُ فِي الْمَكْتَبَةِ.
Playing in the library is forbidden.
sections.cite: Course text written for this lesson (generic; no real person, institution or number). Written in the register of a form with a notice (labels, colons, blanks, يُرْجَى, مَمْنُوعٌ).
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: What is this form for?
items.ar_q: لِمَاذَا هَذِهِ الِاسْتِمَارَةُ؟
options: Please write the name and the address clearly.
items.model: Registering at the library.

items.en: Which lines must you fill in? Name three.
items.ar_q: أَيُّ الْأَسْطُرِ تَمْلَؤُهَا؟ اُذْكُرْ ثَلَاثَةً.
items.model: Any three of: the name, the address, the appointment (day and time), the signature.

items.ar: يُرْجَى كِتَابَةُ الِاسْمِ وَالْعُنْوَانِ كِتَابَةً وَاضِحَةً
items.en: What does this line ask of you?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا يَطْلُبُ هَذَا السَّطْرُ مِنْكَ؟
options: Please write the name and the address clearly.
items.answer: Please write the name and the address clearly.
items.model: Please write the name and the address clearly.

items.en: ★ What does this sign say? What kind of word is مَمْنُوعٌ?
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا تَقُولُ هَذِهِ اللَّافِتَةُ؟ وَمَا نَوْعُ كَلِمَةِ «مَمْنُوعٌ»؟
items.model: Playing in the library is forbidden. مَمْنُوعٌ is “forbidden”, the usual word of signs (a passive participle of the root م ن ع).

items.en: ★ Which three of the ten questions does the form ask you? Say which line answers each.
items.ar_q: ★ أَيُّ ثَلَاثَةِ أَسْئِلَةٍ مِنَ الْعَشَرَةِ تَسْأَلُكَ الِاسْتِمَارَةُ؟
options: Please write the name and the address clearly.
items.model: Who (the name), where (the address), when (the appointment).

sections.name: J
sections.en: In the kitchen. A recipe. Read it, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: طَرِيقَةُ التَّمْرِ بِاللَّبَنِ
Method: dates with milk
الْمَقَادِيرُ: كُوبٌ مِنَ اللَّبَنِ، وَثَلَاثُ تَمَرَاتٍ، وَمِلْعَقَةٌ مِنَ الْعَسَلِ.
Ingredients: a cup of milk, three dates and a spoon of honey.
١. اِغْسِلِ التَّمْرَ جَيِّدًا، ثُمَّ اخْلِطْهُ مَعَ الْعَسَلِ فِي كُوبٍ.
1. Wash the dates well, then mix them with the honey in a cup.
٢. أَضِفِ اللَّبَنَ، ثُمَّ اتْرُكْهُ دَقِيقَتَيْنِ.
2. Add the milk, then leave it for two minutes.
٣. اشْرَبْهُ بَارِدًا.
3. Drink it cold.
sections.cite: Course text written for this lesson (generic; no real person, institution or number). Written in the register of a recipe (ingredients, numbered commands).
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults and older students; children may skip them.

items.en: What are the ingredients?
items.ar_q: مَا الْمَقَادِيرُ؟
options: A cup of milk, three dates and a spoon of honey.
items.answer: A cup of milk, three dates and a spoon of honey.
items.model: A cup of milk, three dates and a spoon of honey.

items.en: How many steps are there, and how are they marked?
items.ar_q: كَمْ خُطْوَةً؟ وَكَيْفَ رُقِّمَتْ؟
options: A cup of milk, three dates and a spoon of honey.
items.model: Three, marked with the digits ١ ٢ ٣.

items.en: In step 2, how long do you leave it?
items.ar_q: فِي الْخُطْوَةِ ٢: كَمْ تَتْرُكُهُ؟
options: A cup of milk, three dates and a spoon of honey.
items.model: Two minutes (دَقِيقَتَيْنِ).

items.en: ★ How can you tell that every step is a command to one person?
items.ar_q: ★ كَيْفَ تَعْرِفُ أَنَّ كُلَّ خُطْوَةٍ أَمْرٌ لِشَخْصٍ وَاحِدٍ؟
items.model: Each step begins with a command verb with no doer written: اِغْسِلْ، اِخْلِطْ، أَضِفْ، اُتْرُكْ، اِشْرَبْ. It speaks to “you”.

items.en: ★ Say the recipe in one line.
items.ar_q: ★ قُلِ الطَّرِيقَةَ كُلَّهَا فِي سَطْرٍ.
items.model: Mix washed dates with honey, add milk, wait two minutes and drink it cold.

sections.name: K
sections.en: At the rawḥa. A fable. Read it, then answer. (★ rows are for adults.)
lines: زَعَمُوا أَنَّ سُلَحْفَاةً وَقِرْدًا كَانَا صَدِيقَيْنِ فِي الْوَادِي.
They claim that a tortoise and a monkey were friends in the wadi.
وَكَانَ الْقِرْدُ يَضْحَكُ مِنْهَا لِأَنَّهَا تَمْشِي قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا.
And the monkey used to laugh at her because she walks little by little.
فَقَالَتْ لَهُ: نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْعَيْنِ وَنَنْظُرُ مَنْ يَصِلُ أَوَّلًا.
So she said to him: Let us go to the spring and see who arrives first.
فَذَهَبَ الْقِرْدُ وَنَامَ تَحْتَ شَجَرَةٍ، وَذَهَبَتِ السُّلَحْفَاةُ قَلِيلًا قَلِيلًا حَتَّى وَصَلَتْ إِلَى الْعَيْنِ.
The monkey went and slept under a tree, and the tortoise went little by little until she reached the spring.
فَرَجَعَ الْقِرْدُ فَرَأَى السُّلَحْفَاةَ هُنَاكَ. وَالْعِبْرَةُ: مَنْ صَبَرَ وَصَلَ.
The monkey came back and saw her there. And the moral: whoever is patient arrives.

lines: النَّحْلُ: هُوَ حَيَوَانٌ صَغِيرٌ يَسْكُنُ فِي بُيُوتٍ كَثِيرَةٍ عَلَى الشَّجَرِ وَفِي الْجَبَلِ.
The bee: it is a small animal that lives in many houses on trees and in the mountain.
وَيَصْنَعُ النَّحْلُ الْعَسَلَ مِنْ أَزْهَارِ النَّبَاتِ.

lines: خَرَجْنَا مِنَ الْمَدِينَةِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَرَكِبْنَا السَّيَّارَةَ.
We went out from the town in the morning and got into the car.
وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى السَّاحِلِ بَعْدَ ثَلَاثِ سَاعَاتٍ، وَأَقَمْنَا فِي الْمِينَاءِ يَوْمَيْنِ.
We arrived at the coast after three hours, and stayed in the port for two days.
ثُمَّ رَكِبْنَا الْبَحْرَ إِلَى بِلَادٍ بَعِيدَةٍ.
Then we embarked on the sea for a far-off land.

lines: ذَهَبَ وَلَدٌ إِلَى مَسْجِدٍ.
vnpn
A boy went to a mosque.
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
vnpn
The boy sat in the mosque.
فَتَحَ الْوَلَدُ مُصْحَفًا.
vnn
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمُصْحَفِ.
vnpn
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
سَجَدَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ.
vnpn
The boy prostrated in prayer.
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ.
vnpn
The boy sat in the study circle.
ذَهَبَ الْأَصْحَابُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ.
vnpn
The friends went to the mosque.
قَرَأَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الْكُتُبِ.
vnpn
The students read in the books.
جَلَسَ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
vnpn
The Habib sat in the mosque.
فَتَحَ الْحَبِيبُ هَذَا الْمُصْحَفَ.
vnnn
The Habib opened this muṣḥaf.
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ هُنَاكَ.
vnn
The boy sat there.
أَيْنَ جَلَسَ الْحَبِيبُ؟
nvn
Where did the Habib sit?
الْمَسْجِدُ كَبِيرٌ.
nn
The mosque is big.
الْحَبِيبُ كَرِيمٌ.
nn
The Habib is kind.
الرَّوْحَةُ طَيِّبَةٌ.
nn
The rawḥa is pleasant.
الْكُتُبُ كَثِيرَةٌ.
nn
The books are many.
هَذِهِ الْحَلْقَةُ كَبِيرَةٌ.
nnn
This study circle is big.
هَذَا النُّورُ جَمِيلٌ.
nnn
This light is beautiful.
الْمَسْجِدُ الْقَدِيمُ نَظِيفٌ.
nnn
The old mosque is clean.
الْحَبِيبُ رَجُلٌ صَالِحٌ.
nnn
The Habib is a righteous man.
أَحْمَدُ وَلَدٌ صَغِيرٌ.
nnn
Ahmad is a small boy.
فَاطِمَةُ أُمٌّ صَالِحَةٌ.
nnn
Fatima is a righteous mother.
أَحْمَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
npn
Ahmad is in the mosque.
الْمَسْجِدُ فِي تَرِيمَ.
npn
The mosque is in Tarim.
هَلِ الْحَبِيبُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ؟
pnpn
Is the Habib in the mosque?
نَعَمْ، الْحَبِيبُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
pnpn
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
الدَّرْسُ طَوِيلٌ.
nn
The lesson is long.
لَيْسَ الدَّرْسُ صَعْبًا.
vnn
The lesson is not difficult.
ذَهَبَ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ.
vpn
He went to the rawḥa.
رَجَعَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ.
vpn
He returned to the house.
دَخَلَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْبَابِ.
vnpn
The boy came in through the door.
نَظَرَتِ الْأُمُّ إِلَى الْوَلَدِ.
vnpn
The mother looked at the boy.
هَلْ ذَهَبْتَ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
pvpn
“Did you go to the rawḥa?”
نَعَمْ، ذَهَبْتُ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ.
pvpn
“Yes, I went to the rawḥa.”
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ.
vnn
The boy memorised the lesson.
خَدَمَ الْوَلَدُ الضُّيُوفَ.
vnn
The boy served the guests.
يَجْلِسُ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ الْيَوْمَ.
vnpnn
The boy sits in the study circle today.
تَقْرَأُ مَرْيَمُ الْمُصْحَفَ الْآنَ.
vnnn
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
هُمْ يَحْضُرُونَ الرَّوْحَةَ.
nvn
They attend the rawḥa.
أَنَا أَحْفَظُ الدَّرْسَ.
nvn
“I am memorising the lesson.”
اِجْلِسْ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
vpn
“Sit in the majlis (the gathering).”
لَا تَخْرُجْ مِنَ الْمَجْلِسِ.
pvpn
“Do not leave the majlis.”
كَانَ الْوَلَدُ سَعِيدًا فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
vnnpn
The boy was happy in the majlis.
كَانَتْ مَرْيَمُ سَعِيدَةً فِي الْحَلْقَةِ.
vnnpn
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
لَمْ يَخْرُجِ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْمَجْلِسِ.
pvnpn
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
pvnpnn
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
vnpnpn
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ بِأَدَبٍ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
vnnpn
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
فَتَحَ الْوَلَدُ مُصْحَفَهُ.
vnn
The boy opened his muṣḥaf.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ الرَّاتِبَ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
vnnpn
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
vnpnpnn
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي حَلْقَةِ الذِّكْرِ.
vnpnn
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
سَأَلَهُ الْحَبِيبُ عَنِ الدَّرْسِ.
vnpn
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
فَهِمَهُ الْوَلَدُ.
vn
The boy understood it.
خَدَمَ الْوَلَدُ الضُّيُوفَ وَحَمَلَ الطَّعَامَ.
vnnvn
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
pvnpnvn
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
شَكَرَ الضُّيُوفُ الْوَلَدَ الَّذِي خَدَمَهُمْ.
vnnnv
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
vnnvpn
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
vnnpvn
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
pnnnvnnn
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
vnpnpn
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: الْعِلْمُ نُورٌ.
vnnn
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
vnnpnnpn
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
vnpnvnpnn
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
فَتَحَ الْوَلَدُ مُصْحَفَهُ وَقَرَأَ وِرْدَهُ.
vnnvn
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
vnpnpv
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
vnnpnnppn
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
vnnnnnn
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
حَمِدَ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ اللَّهَ.
vnnn
The boy’s father praised Allah.
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
vnpnnpn
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
vpnvpn
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
قِيلَ لِلْوَلَدِ: الْعِلْمُ نُورٌ.
vnnn
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
vnnnvvpnnp
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
ذَكَّرَ الْوَلَدُ صَدِيقَهُ بِالصَّلَاةِ.
vnnn
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
pnvnpnvn
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
vnnnnnn
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
pnnvnpnpn
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
سَاعَدَ الْوَلَدُ الضُّيُوفَ وَأَكْرَمَهُمْ.
vnnv
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
تَعَاوَنَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الرِّبَاطِ.
vnpn
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
تَوَاضَعَ الْوَلَدُ وَتَعَلَّمَ مِنْهُمْ.
vnvp
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
vnnpnn
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
vnpnvnpn
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
vnnpvpn
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
vnnpnvn
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ حَدِيثًا بِسَنَدِهِ.
vnnn
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
vnvvpvnppnn
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
vnpnvnpvvnv
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
قَامَ الْوَلَدُ وَقَالَ: آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ.
vnvvn
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.

The boy went with his father to the wadi and saw many date palms.
وَالنَّخْلَةُ شَجَرَةٌ ثَمَرُهَا طَيِّبٌ، وَعِنْدَهَا عَيْنُ مَاءٍ.
nnnnpnn
The date palm is a tree whose fruit is good, and by it is a spring of water.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ كِتَابَ تَارِيخٍ عَنْ تَأْسِيسِ تَرِيمَ.
vnnnpnn
The boy read a history book about the founding of Tarim.
وَقَرَأَ: أُسِّسَتْ تَرِيمُ قَبْلَ وَقْتٍ طَوِيلٍ.
vvnpnn
And he read: Tarim was founded a long time ago.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي رِحْلَتِهِ: خَرَجْنَا مِنْ تَرِيمَ مَعَ أَبِي وَعُمَرَ وَوَصَلْنَا إِلَى الشِّحْرِ.
vnpnvpnpnnvpn
The boy wrote on his journey: We left Tarim with my father and Umar, and we arrived at al-Shiḥr.
أَقَمْنَا أَيَّامًا عَلَى السَّاحِلِ وَرَأَيْنَا الْمِينَاءَ.
vnpnvn
We stayed some days on the coast, and we saw the port.
فِي مُقَابَلَةٍ سَأَلَ الْوَلَدُ الْخَزَّافَ: كَيْفَ تَبْدَأُ عَمَلَكَ؟
pnvnnnvn
In an interview the boy asked the potter: How do you begin your work?
فَقَالَ الْخَزَّافُ: أَبْدَأُ بِالطِّينِ وَالْمَاءِ، وَهَذِهِ حِرْفَةُ أَبِي.
vnvnnnnn
The potter said: I begin with clay and water, and this is my father’s craft.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ عَقْدًا بَيْنَ سَالِمٍ وَعَلِيٍّ، وَكَانَ شَاهِدًا.
vnnpnnvn
The boy wrote a contract between Salim and Ali, and he was a witness.
بَاعَ سَالِمٌ لِعَلِيٍّ تَمْرًا بِثَمَنٍ قَدْرُهُ مِائَةُ رِيَالٍ.
vnnnnnnn
Salim sold dates to Ali for a price amounting to one hundred riyals.
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي صَمْتٍ عَلَى السَّاحِلِ وَشَعَرَ بِفَرَحٍ وَحُزْنٍ.
vnpnpnvnn
The boy sat in silence on the coast and felt joy and sadness.
وَقَالَ فِي نَفْسِهِ: مَتَى أَرْجِعُ إِلَى أُمِّي وَإِلَى تَرِيمَ؟
vpnnvpnpn
And he said to himself: When shall I return to my mother and to Tarim?
رَجَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى تَرِيمَ وَجَلَسَ مَعَ وُلَيْدٍ صَغِيرٍ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ.
vnpnvpnnpn
The boy returned to Tarim and sat with a little boy in the mosque.
وَعَلَّمَهُ أَوَّلَ دَرْسٍ: اِقْرَأْ وَافْهَمْ.
vnnvv
And he taught him the first lesson: Read and understand.
